input.body:
Prose-to-checks sweep over `.claudinite/local/packs` (the only pack path in scope; nothing under `.claudinite/shared/` was touched). Tracking issue #116.

## The prose

`browser-speech/RULES.md`, "Endpointing is unreliable — plan for the miss":

> …with interim results used **only** as the "still speaking" signal, never delivered to the caller.

Always-testable — it constrains a static signature in the source — and no existing check covered it. The pack's five existing checks are about TTS settling, STT terminal handlers, mic release, mic constraints and the error mapping's totality; none look at what the result handler does with an interim hypothesis.

The rest of that paragraph is *not* convertible (the pause monitor's existence, the measured window), and neither is the rest of the remaining prose — the `chrome.tts`-in-content-scripts relay, the preflight, contextual biasing and voice selection are API-surface choices, best-effort behaviour, and taste. This is the one static signature left in the file.

## The check

**`stt-interim-results-gated`** (blocking). A file that turns `interimResults` on *and wires the `result` event itself* must reference `isFinal`. Interim hypotheses arrive on the **same** `result` event as the finished utterance — enabling the flag opens no second channel — and `isFinal` is the only thing in the Web Speech API that tells the two apart. A handler without it hands the caller a half-heard fragment, then the next one, several times per utterance: the `"heart heart"` shape the pause monitor exists to prevent, with nothing thrown and nothing logged and a transcript that even looks plausible.

Narrow on purpose, three ways — each killing a false alarm a whole-file grep makes:

1. The **assigned value** is read. `interimResults = false` (or `0`/`null`/`undefined`) turns the flag off, every result is then final, and firing there is pure noise. Anything else counts as on — including a computed flag (`rec.interimResults = pauseResetMs > 0`, the shape real code takes), because a check cannot show it is false and the handler must survive it being true.
2. Only a file that **wires `result` itself** is judged. A config module that sets the flag and hands the recognizer on has its gate in whatever file reads the results; the rule has no honest opinion about a handler it cannot see.
3. Comments are **stripped first**, so a comment naming the trap — the check's own header included — cannot fire it.

`isFinal` anywhere in the file counts as the gate: there is no second spelling to look for, and reading it at all means the distinction was considered.

## See-it-fail, in both directions

Per the pack README's rule that a precision-critical check has to prove the parsing was *necessary*:

- **Red first** — the 3 firing fixtures (property assignment; the object-literal form + `addEventListener` wiring in TypeScript; the computed flag) were written and run before the module existed.
- **Neutered `isFinal` gate** → the clean fixture fails **and so does this repo's own `extension/src/speech/stt-port.js`** — which is what proves the rule actually reaches the real file rather than passing over it. Restored, both are quiet: `stt-port.js` sets `rec.interimResults = pauseResetMs > 0` and gates on `results[i].isFinal !== false`.
- **Naive "mentions `interimResults`, never `isFinal`" grep** → the flag-off, config-module and comment-only fixtures all *wrongly fire*. That is what earns the value-reading, the `result`-wiring gate and the comment strip their complexity; asserted directly in `pack.test.mjs`.

## Deletion test

The endpointing paragraph in `RULES.md` **stays whole**. The check proves an interim result is distinguished and nothing more; that Chrome mis-endpoints at all, that the remedy is a pause monitor which discards and reopens, the measured 1.2 s vs 1.8 s window (this product's number, to be re-measured elsewhere), and the caveat about an audible reset cue are all carried only by the prose. Per the test's discriminating half, a paragraph carrying what the check does not stays — so it gains a pointer to the check, not a trim. `README.md`'s check/prose tables, the "all five scan" count and the parsed-not-grepped section are updated for the sixth rule.

`npm test` green: **411 tests across 20 files**, including the pack's 51 fixtures. `check_the_world` is 0 blocking (7 pre-existing `file-placement` advisories, untouched).

Not auto-merged — a check can break CI or misfire, so this task's ceiling is open-pr and it is left for owner review.

{"number":117,"title":"Claudinite growth: convert the interim-results rule to a check (#116)","body":"Prose-to-checks sweep over `.claudinite/local/packs` (the only pack path in scope; nothing under `.claudinite/shared/` was touched). Tracking issue #116.

## The prose

`browser-speech/RULES.md`, "Endpointing is unreliable — plan for the miss":

> …with interim results used **only** as the "still speaking" signal, never delivered to the caller.

Always-testable — it constrains a static signature in the source — and no existing check covered it. The pack's five existing checks are about TTS settling, STT terminal handlers, mic release, mic constraints and the error mapping's totality; none look at what the result handler does with an interim hypothesis.

The rest of that paragraph is *not* convertible (the pause monitor's existence, the measured window), and neither is the rest of the remaining prose — the `chrome.tts`-in-content-scripts relay, the preflight, contextual biasing and voice selection are API-surface choices, best-effort behaviour, and taste. This is the one static signature left in the file.

## The check

**`stt-interim-results-gated`** (blocking). A file that turns `interimResults` on *and wires the `result` event itself* must reference `isFinal`. Interim hypotheses arrive on the **same** `result` event as the finished utterance — enabling the flag opens no second channel — and `isFinal` is the only thing in the Web Speech API that tells the two apart. A handler without it hands the caller a half-heard fragment, then the next one, several times per utterance: the `"heart heart"` shape the pause monitor exists to prevent, with nothing thrown and nothing logged and a transcript that even looks plausible.

Narrow on purpose, three ways — each killing a false alarm a whole-file grep makes:

1. The **assigned value** is read. `interimResults = false` (or `0`/`null`/`undefined`) turns the flag off, every result is then final, and firing there is pure noise. Anything else counts as on — including a computed flag (`rec.interimResults = pauseResetMs > 0`, the shape real code takes), because a check cannot show it is false and the handler must survive it being true.
2. Only a file that **wires `result` itself** is judged. A config module that sets the flag and hands the recognizer on has its gate in whatever file reads the results; the rule has no honest opinion about a handler it cannot see.
3. Comments are **stripped first**, so a comment naming the trap — the check's own header included — cannot fire it.

`isFinal` anywhere in the file counts as the gate: there is no second spelling to look for, and reading it at all means the distinction was considered.

## See-it-fail, in both directions

Per the pack README's rule that a precision-critical check has to prove the parsing was *necessary*:

- **Red first** — the 3 firing fixtures (property assignment; the object-literal form + `addEventListener` wiring in TypeScript; the computed flag) were written and run before the module existed.
- **Neutered `isFinal` gate** → the clean fixture fails **and so does this repo's own `extension/src/speech/stt-port.js`** — which is what proves the rule actually reaches the real file rather than passing over it. Restored, both are quiet: `stt-port.js` sets `rec.interimResults = pauseResetMs > 0` and gates on `results[i].isFinal !== false`.
- **Naive "mentions `interimResults`, never `isFinal`" grep** → the flag-off, config-module and comment-only fixtures all *wrongly fire*. That is what earns the value-reading, the `result`-wiring gate and the comment strip their complexity; asserted directly in `pack.test.mjs`.

## Deletion test

The endpointing paragraph in `RULES.md` **stays whole**. The check proves an interim result is distinguished and nothing more; that Chrome mis-endpoints at all, that the remedy is a pause monitor which discards and reopens, the measured 1.2 s vs 1.8 s window (this product's number, to be re-measured elsewhere), and the caveat about an audible reset cue are all carried only by the prose. Per the test's discriminating half, a paragraph carrying what the check does not stays — so it gains a pointer to the check, not a trim. `README.md`'s check/prose tables, the "all five scan" count and the parsed-not-grepped section are updated for the sixth rule.

## Verification

`npm test` green: **411 tests across 20 files**, including the pack's 51 fixtures. `check_the_world` is 0 blocking (7 pre-existing `file-placement` advisories, untouched).

Not auto-merged — a check can break CI or misfire, so this task's ceiling is open-pr and it is left for owner review.
